title: Mailchimp Pricing in 2026: Full Breakdown and Hidden Costs
summary: Mailchimp pricing tiers shift based on your active subscriber count and monthly email volume. Use this breakdown to forecast your annual marketing budget.
body_markdown:
## Mailchimp pricing plans and monthly costs for 2026


Mailchimp's 2026 pricing runs from a free plan to Premium at $350+ per month, and it's based on total contacts stored, not emails sent. Paid plans start at $13+ for Essentials and $20+ for Standard. Premium has unlimited contacts and a 15x send multiplier.


[Mailchimp](https://mailchimp.com/pricing/marketing) ’s 2026 pricing structure scales from a $0 Free tier to a $350+ Premium tier. It bases every dollar you spend on the **total number of contacts** stored rather than the number of active customers you're actually engaging.


This model forces you to choose between paying for "dead" data or spending manual hours pruning lists to avoid the next pricing bracket.


### The 2026 Mailchimp pricing table


The following table breaks down the entry-level costs and volume caps. It shows how quickly a growing list triggers a mandatory migration to higher monthly overhead.


Plan Starting Price Contact Cap Monthly Send Limit


Free $0 250 500 (2x multiplier)


Essentials $13+ 50,000 10x multiplier


Standard $20+ 100,000 12x multiplier


Premium $350+ Unlimited 15x multiplier


*Prices and plan limits checked against[mailchimp.com](https://mailchimp.com/pricing/marketing) on September 27, 2026.*


These tiers dictate the fundamental ceiling of your marketing reach before the platform requires a plan upgrade.


### Mailchimp free plan contact limits


When a single successful lead-generation campaign hits, the Free plan’s **250-contact cap** can push a small business into a paid tier overnight.


With a 2x email send multiplier, PriceTimeline notes that a user with a full list can only contact their audience twice per month, so frequent engagement with subscribers is effectively throttled.


High-frequency weekly newsletters or complex automated sequences are effectively prohibited by this restriction.


### Essentials vs. Standard: The mid-market choice


Mailchimp advertises the Standard plan at a $17 promotional rate for 12 months. This is a temporary discount before the price reverts to the $20 baseline, so you'll need to budget for a future cost increase.


Everboost’s analysis puts this $20 entry point for 1,000 contacts in the middle of the market, so users can expect neither the lowest possible price nor the highest premium.


It's more expensive than ActiveCampaign’s $19 or Brevo’s $9, but remains cheaper than Klaviyo ($30), Constant Contact ($35), or ConvertKit ($39), positioning the service as a mid-range choice for cost-conscious marketers who are comparing entry-level costs across the industry, meaning it serves as a compromise between budget-friendly platforms and premium competitors, worth weighing against other[Mailchimp alternatives](https://www.activepieces.com/blog/10-best-mailchimp-alternatives-for-email-marketing) .


The primary difference between these tiers's the volume of activity permitted per contact. Essentials offers a 10x send multiplier, restricting a 1,000-contact list to 10,000 total monthly sends, effectively capping the frequency of communication for small lists.


Standard increases this to a 12x multiplier, providing two extra sends per contact for those running more aggressive multi-step campaigns, thereby allowing for more complex customer journeys that require multiple touchpoints, which grants marketers greater flexibility in their outreach strategy.


Standard also includes behavioral targeting, which's necessary if you intend to use[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) to automate list management based on external CRM signals.


Activepieces is an MIT-licensed AI automation platform that connects to 735+ integrations, allowing you to sync these behavioral segments to other tools without manual exports.


### The technical wall in the Essentials tier


The requirement for the Standard plan when using external CRM signals stems from the lack of Advanced Segmentation in the Essentials tier. Essentials users are restricted to basic logic, which prevents the platform from processing complex incoming data points from third-party tools in real-time.


Without these behavioral targeting features, Mailchimp cannot dynamically sort contacts into specific buckets based on actions taken outside of its own ecosystem.


This forces users to pay a higher monthly rate just to unlock the data pathways that allow external signals to influence their marketing automation.


### Mailchimp Premium plan pricing and features


Starting at $350, the Premium plan represents a significant jump that buys a **15x send multiplier** and removes the hard contact caps found in lower tiers, meaning high-volume senders no longer have to worry about hitting arbitrary usage ceilings. **This allows high-volume senders to scale without hitting artificial platform restrictions.**


Mailchimp built this tier for high-volume senders who require a dedicated IP to protect their deliverability. The cost continues to scale with contact count, and even enterprise users pay for inactive subscribers.
